2.name: second person
2.plain: the person or people spoken to: you

3.name: third person
3.plain: someone else: he, she, they (only on the independent pronouns yeye and wao; on verbs, third persons are glossed by class, C1 and C2)

PL.name: plural
PL.plain: more than one; on commands and object forms, the -ni that adds 'you all'

COP.name: copula
COP.plain: the linking word ni: 'is, are, am', the same for every person

NEG.name: negative
NEG.plain: marks 'not': the copula si, the ha- of negative verbs, the final -i of the negative present and the -si- of negative subjunctives, relatives and conditions

C1.name: class 1
C1.plain: the singular class of people (m-/mw-: mtu 'person'); as a verb prefix, 'he' or 'she'

C2.name: class 2
C2.plain: the plural class of people (wa-: watu 'people'); as a verb prefix, 'they'

SM.name: subject marker
SM.plain: the prefix at the front of a verb that says who or what the subject is (ni-, u-, a-, ki-, zi- ...)

PRS.name: present
PRS.plain: the -na- tense: happening now, or generally

FV.name: final vowel
FV.plain: the last slot of a Bantu verb, normally -a; it changes to -e for the subjunctive and -i for the negative present

INF.name: infinitive
INF.plain: the ku- form that names the action: kusoma 'to read, reading'

Q.name: question particle
Q.plain: je, the word that announces a question

C16.name: class 16
C16.plain: the pa- place class: a definite spot, 'at, on' (hapa 'here', mahali 'place') Also used alone for the place suffixes -po, -ko, -mo (nipo 'I am here').

C17.name: class 17
C17.plain: the ku- place class: a general area or a direction, 'around, to, from' (huku, kule) Also used alone for the place suffixes -po, -ko, -mo (nipo 'I am here').

C18.name: class 18
C18.plain: the mu- place class: inside, 'in, within' (humu, mle) Also used alone for the place suffixes -po, -ko, -mo (nipo 'I am here').

C7.name: class 7
C7.plain: the singular ki- class (kitabu 'book'): many objects, tools, languages, diminutives

C8.name: class 8
C8.plain: the plural vi- class (vitabu 'books'), plural of class 7

C3.name: class 3
C3.plain: the singular m- class of trees, plants, body parts and natural forces (mti 'tree')

C4.name: class 4
C4.plain: the plural mi- class (miti 'trees'), plural of class 3

C5.name: class 5
C5.plain: the singular ji- class, often with no visible prefix (jicho 'eye', gari 'car')

C6.name: class 6
C6.plain: the ma- class: plural of class 5, and liquids and masses (maji 'water')

C9.name: class 9
C9.plain: the singular nasal class, often with no visible prefix (nyumba 'house', meza 'table')

C10.name: class 10
C10.plain: the plural of classes 9 and 11, usually looking the same as class 9 (nyumba 'houses')

C11.name: class 11
C11.plain: the singular u- class of long or flat things (ukuta 'wall'), plural in class 10

C14.name: class 14
C14.plain: the u- class of abstract nouns (uhuru 'freedom', utoto 'childhood')

ANA.name: anaphoric demonstrative
ANA.plain: the -o demonstrative (huyo, hicho): 'that one just mentioned', or something near the listener

LOC.name: locative
LOC.plain: the suffix -ni that turns a noun into a place: nyumbani 'at home'

KU.name: ku of short verbs
KU.plain: the syllable ku kept by two-syllable verbs (kula, kunywa) after tense markers that cannot carry the stress

PRF.name: perfect
PRF.plain: the -me- tense: it has happened and the result still holds; with NEG, the -ja- of 'not yet'

OM.name: object marker
OM.plain: the prefix just before the verb root that says who or what the object is (-ni- 'me', -ki- 'it, class 7')

SBJV.name: subjunctive
SBJV.plain: the form with final -e: 'let me, that you should, so that'

C15.name: class 15
C15.plain: the ku- class of infinitives used as nouns (kusoma 'reading')

HAB.name: habitual
HAB.plain: the prefix hu- of what usually or always happens; it takes no subject prefix

SIT.name: situational
SIT.plain: the -ki- tense of background situations: 'while, if, when'

CONS.name: consecutive
CONS.plain: the -ka- tense of the next event in a story: 'and then'

REL.name: relative
REL.plain: the 'o of reference' (-ye-, -cho-, -po- ...) or amba- that makes a 'who, which, where, when' clause

FOC.name: focus
FOC.plain: the ndi- of 'it is X (and no one else)': ndiye, ndicho

CTRF.name: counterfactual
CTRF.plain: the -ngali- of 'would have' for things that did not happen

APPL.name: applicative
APPL.plain: the verb suffix -i-/-e- (-li-/-le-) that adds 'for, to, at, about': -nunulia 'buy for'

PASS.name: passive
PASS.plain: the verb suffix -w- (-iw-, -liw-...) that makes the object the subject: 'is done'

CAUS.name: causative
CAUS.plain: the verb suffix -ish-/-esh- or -iz-/-ez- that means 'make do, cause': -somesha 'teach'

STAT.name: stative
STAT.plain: the verb suffix -ik-/-ek- of a change with no agent, or of possibility: -vunjika 'get broken'

RECP.name: reciprocal
RECP.plain: the verb suffix -an- 'each other': -pendana 'love each other'

REV.name: reversive
REV.plain: the verb suffix -u-/-o- that undoes the action: -fungua 'open' from -funga 'shut'

GNO.name: gnomic
GNO.plain: the -a- tense (nasoma, twaenda): a general or timeless present, now mostly written

terms.lingua franca: A language used for communication between speakers of different languages (swh-00-01).
terms.Bantu: A large family of African languages that share noun classes and verb-building patterns (swh-00-01).
terms.tone: Pitch used to tell words apart; Swahili has lost it, unlike most Bantu languages (swh-00-01).
terms.noun class: One of the groups into which every noun falls, each with its own prefixes and agreement (swh-00-02).
terms.agreement: Other words in the sentence taking a prefix that matches the noun's class (swh-00-02).
terms.verb template: The fixed order of slots in which a Swahili verb is built (swh-00-02).
terms.slot: One position in the verb template, filled by one kind of piece (swh-00-02).
terms.gloss: The line under an example that labels each piece of each word (swh-00-02).
terms.agglutinative: Built by stringing pieces together, each with one meaning (swh-00-02).
terms.subject prefix: The piece at the front of a verb that shows the subject's person or class (SM) (swh-00-03).
terms.object prefix: The OM slot before the root (swh-04-07).
terms.syllable: A beat of a word, built round one vowel (swh-01-01).
terms.open syllable: A syllable that ends in a vowel, the normal Swahili shape (swh-01-01).
terms.syllabic nasal: An m or n that forms a syllable on its own, as in mtu (swh-01-01).
terms.digraph: Two letters spelling one sound, such as ch or ng' (swh-01-02).
terms.implosive: A b, d, j or g said by drawing air inwards, heard at the coast (swh-01-02).
terms.prenasalised: A consonant begun with a nasal in the same syllable, such as mb or nd (swh-01-03).
terms.stress: The extra force that makes one syllable stand out (swh-01-05).
terms.penult: The second-from-last syllable of a word (swh-01-05).
terms.glide: A w or y sound formed when a vowel runs into another vowel (swh-01-06).
terms.coalescence: Two vowels merging into one when a prefix meets a stem (swh-01-06).
terms.yes-no question: A question answered yes or no (swh-02-04).
terms.place classes: Classes 16, 17 and 18 (pa-, ku-, mu-): definite place, general place, inside (swh-02-05).
terms.imperative: The command form of the verb (swh-02-07).
terms.concord: The agreement prefix a word takes to match a noun's class (swh-03-01).
terms.animate agreement: Animals and people taking class 1/2 agreement whatever their noun class (swh-03-09).
terms.anaphoric: Pointing back to something already mentioned, as the -o demonstratives do (swh-03-12).
terms.o of reference: The -o form (-yo, -cho, -vyo…) that refers back to a noun already mentioned (swh-03-14).
terms.nominal agreement: The agreement prefixes adjectives take, close to the noun prefixes (swh-03-15).
terms.pronominal agreement: The agreement prefixes of possessives, demonstratives, the -a of 'of' and reference forms, close to the verb's subject prefixes (swh-03-15).
terms.marker: A piece in one slot of the verb template (preferred here to 'infix') (swh-04-01).
terms.perfect: The -me- tense for a completed action with present relevance (swh-04-05).
terms.inchoative: A verb meaning 'become' whose perfect describes a state (swh-04-06).
terms.subjunctive: The -e form for wishes, requests and purposes (swh-04-10).
terms.infinitive: The ku- form, also a verbal noun (swh-04-12).
terms.habitual: The hu- form for what usually happens (swh-04-13).
terms.consecutive: The -ka- form for the next step in a sequence (swh-04-15).
terms.compound tense: A tense built with an auxiliary verb such as -wa (swh-04-16).
terms.invariable adjective: An adjective that takes no class prefix, such as safi or ghali (swh-05-01).
terms.ornative: A word meaning 'having' or 'with', such as -enye (swh-05-02).
terms.reduplication: Saying a word twice to change its force, such as polepole (swh-05-07).
terms.derivation: Making a new word from an existing root with a prefix or suffix (swh-05-11).
terms.diminutive: A noun moved into class 7/8 to mean a small one (swh-05-11).
terms.augmentative: A noun moved into class 5/6 to mean a big one (swh-05-11).
